correctness.rationale: Theorem 5.8 of Kazemifard–Tafazolian, inspected in its original source, provides the smooth characteristic-2 genus-6 C12 cover and two distinct branch inertia orders 12 and 3; these are expressly premises. A pair conjugacy descends to z->az, since full wild and tame branch points must be fixed. Equality of the unique quadratic Artin–Schreier quotient class of t=1/z forces a=1 by odd pole order, excluding all nonidentity base scalings. Over this fixed base, the cubic C3 subextension is the same; the cyclic C4 Witt class (t,lambda*t) is unique up to units +1,-1. In characteristic two, - (t,lambda*t)=(t,lambda*t+t²), Witt addition has cross term first_coordinates_product, and F-1 of (0,t)=(0,t²+t). Positive-unit equality forces mu=lambda; negative-unit equality forces mu=lambda+1. No other coboundary is possible by the same pole parity/degree comparison. Thus the pair invariant lambda²+lambda has exactly two-element fibres and is onto an algebraically closed field. The normalizer descending trivially lies in the deck G; reverse inclusion obvious. Independent polynomial ring F2[L,T] Witt calculations and GF16 additive fibre count corroborated identities; infinite-field pole proof is analytic, not experimentally inferred.
